title: Rhizosphere Proton (H+) Exudation and Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) Kinetics under NO3-/NH4+ Dosing
description: PhD dissertation modeling root plasma membrane H+-ATPase proton pumping, rhizosphere pH drift, and substrate CEC under dynamic nitrate-to-ammonium ratios.
image_caption: Rhizosphere pH micro-electrode mapping micro-zone acidification around root hair elongation zones.
overview: Uptake of ammonium (NH4⁺) via root AMT transporters triggers net proton (H⁺) exudation via plasma membrane H⁺-ATPase, acidifying the rhizosphere pH by up to 1.4 units. Conversely, nitrate (NO3⁻) symport utilizes H⁺ co-consumption, elevating rhizosphere pH. This doctoral research formulates a dynamic N-ratio feedback controller: maintaining an NO3⁻:NH4⁺ molar ratio of 11:1 stabilizes substrate pH precisely at 5.85 ± 0.15 without requiring chemical acid/base dosing, optimizing bio-available Iron (Fe²⁺) and Manganese (Mn²⁺) solubility.

climate_strategy.strategy: Install automated inline pH/EC telemetry coupled with dual-stock fertilizer injectors. Dynamically modulate Ammonium Nitrate [PubChem CID 22985] dosing based on 15-minute drain pH feedback.

crop_steering.intro: Rhizosphere pH stabilization and cation uptake matrix.

fertigation.vegetative_phase: Formulate Calcium Nitrate [PubChem CID 24963] (Ca 4.5 mM) and Ammonium Nitrate [PubChem CID 22985] (NH4⁺ 1.0 mM) to drive gentle root acidification.
fertigation.generative_phase: Eliminate NH4⁺ dosing during high root temperature (> 23°C) to prevent root respiration oxygen stress.

references.text: Rhizosphere pH dynamics and cation exchange kinetics under differential nitrate/ammonium fertigation.
